examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Separate union, concatenation and star, and preserve parentheses. A regular expression need not be a unique description of its language. To count short strings in unions, remove duplicates such as epsilon. Expressions encoding odd/even counts may be simpler to understand through a DFA invariant than through expansion.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many binary strings of length 5 match 0*1(0+10*1)*?

**Answer: 16.** The expression accepts exactly strings with an odd number of 1s. Flipping the first bit pairs each even-parity string with an odd-parity string, so half of 2⁵=32 strings qualify: 16.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Star includes zero repetitions; plus means one or more when used as a postfix repetition operator, but + between expressions usually means union in these papers.

The empty language ∅ and the language {ε} are different.
